style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings. Ecclesiastes uses Elohim throughout — the divine name YHWH never appears in the book and is never inserted.
chapterNote: The chapter opens with the book's two hardest truths held in one hand: the righteous and the wise and everything they do are in the hand of God -- and one event still comes to all of them, clean and unclean, worshiper and scoffer alike. From inside that shadow the Preacher issues his fullest, warmest charge to actually live: eat your bread with joy, drink your wine with a glad heart, wear white, keep the oil on your head, love your wife every vapor-day you are given, and whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for Sheol holds no work, no planning, no knowledge, no wisdom. Verse 11 then knocks the props from under every meritocracy: the race does not go to the swift nor bread to the wise, for time and chance meet them all, and like fish in a net men are seized by an hour they never saw coming. The closing parable of the poor wise man who saved a little city and was forgotten distills the whole book on wisdom: better than strength, better than weapons of war -- and one sinner destroys much good.

1.text: For I laid all this to heart, and set myself to sift it all out: that the righteous and the wise, and all their works, rest in the hand of God. Whether love or hatred waits ahead, man does not know; everything lies before them.
1.amp: For all this I considered ['gave, set to my heart', natan, leb, the KJV margin] even to declare all this, that the righteous [tsaddiq], and the wise [chakam], and their works, are in the hand of God [Elohim]: no man [adam] knows [yada] either love [ahavah] or hatred [sinah] by all that is before [panim] them.
1.notes: The anchor sentence of the chapter: the tsaddiq (H6662) and his deeds are held in God's hand -- and the same held man cannot read from his circumstances whether ahavah (H160) or hatred lies in tomorrow. Held, but not shown the file.

2.text: All things come to all alike; one event meets the righteous and the wicked, the good, the clean and the unclean, the one who sacrifices and the one who never does. As with the good man, so with the sinner; the man who swears freely, and the man who trembles at an oath.
2.amp: All things come alike to all: there is one [echad] event to the righteous [tsaddiq], and to the wicked [rasha]; to the good [tov] and to the clean [tahor], and to the unclean [tame]; to him that sacrifices [zabach], and to him that sacrifices not: as is the good, so is the sinner [chet]; and he that swears [shaba], as he that fears [yare] an oath [shebuah].
2.notes: Five matched pairs, moral, ritual, and verbal, all leveled by the one event of death. tahor (H2889) and tame (H2931) are the temple's own clean/unclean line; even that boundary does not reroute the funeral procession.

3.text: This is an evil in everything done under the sun, that one event comes to everyone. And more: the heart of the sons of man is full of evil, madness lives in their heart all their lives, and after that -- to the dead.
3.amp: This is an evil [ra] among all things that are done [asah] under the sun [shemesh], that there is one [echad] event unto all: yea, also the heart [leb] of the sons of men [adam] is full [male] of evil [ra], and madness [holelut] is in their heart [lebab] while they live [chay], and after [achar] that they go to the dead.
3.notes: The leveling breeds the madness: if outcomes do not distinguish, why should conduct? So the leb fills, male (H4390), with ra, and holelut (H1947) takes up residence. The verse's last clause drops like a trapdoor -- and after that, to the dead.

4.text: But whoever is still joined to all the living has hope, for a living dog is better off than a dead lion.
4.amp: For to him that is [yesh] joined [chabar] to all the living [chay] there is hope [bittachon -- confidence, assurance]: for a living dog [kelev] is better [tov] than a dead lion [aryeh].
4.notes: bittachon (H986) is confident hope, and chabar (H2266) the joining-word: mere membership among the living keeps the account open. The dog was despised and the aryeh (H738) royal, yet breath outranks pedigree -- while you live, something can still be done.

5.text: For the living know at least this, that they will die; but the dead know nothing at all, and they have no more wage to collect, for the memory of them is forgotten.
5.amp: For the living [chay] know [yada] that they shall die [muth]: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward [sakar -- wage]; for the memory [zeker] of them is forgotten [shakach].
5.notes: Spoken strictly from under the sun, where observation stops at the grave: the one certainty the living hold, mortality, is itself an advantage, for it can still teach (cf. Psalm 90:12). zeker (H2143) and shakach (H7911): even remembrance, the last earthly wage, expires.

6.text: Their love, their hatred, and their envy have already perished, and never again will they hold a portion in anything done under the sun.
6.amp: Also their love [ahavah], and their hatred [sinah], and their envy [qinah], is now [kebar] perished [abad]; neither have they any more a portion [cheleq] for ever [olam] in any thing that is done [asah] under the sun [shemesh].
6.notes: The three fires that drove a lifetime, ahavah (H160), hatred, and qinah (H7068), the envy-engine of 4:4, all abad (H6), gone out. cheleq (H2506), the portion-word: the dead hold no more shares in the world's doings, which is precisely why the living must spend theirs now.

7.text: Go then, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already accepted your works.
7.amp: Go your way [yalak], eat [akal] your bread [lechem] with joy [simchah], and drink [shatah] your wine [yayin] with a merry [tov] heart [leb]; for God [Elohim] now [kebar -- already] accepts [ratsah -- is pleased with, delights in] your works [maaseh].
7.notes: ratsah (H7521) is the acceptance-word of sacrifices found pleasing: the meal is eaten under smiling heaven, not on probation. kebar, already -- the approval precedes the feast, which turns enjoyment itself into a act of faith in the Giver.

8.text: Let your garments be white at every hour, and let no oil be lacking on your head.
8.amp: Let your garments [beged] be always [et -- at every time] white [laban]; and let your head [rosh] lack [chaser] no ointment [shemen -- oil].
8.notes: White beged (H899) and shemen (H8081) on the rosh were festival dress, the opposite of sackcloth and ashes: the charge is to live festally as the norm, not the exception. chaser (H2637), the lacking-word of 6:2 -- here, at last, something not to lack.

9.text: See life with the wife you love, all the days of your vapor of a life that He has given you under the sun, every vapor-day of it; for this is your portion in life, and in the toil you labor at under the sun.
9.amp: Live joyfully ['See, enjoy life', raah, chay, the KJV margin] with the wife [ishshah] whom you love [ahab] all the days [yom] of the life of your vapor [hebel], which He has given [natan] you under the sun [shemesh], all the days of your vapor: for that is your portion [cheleq] in this life [chay], and in your labour [amal] which you take under the sun.
9.notes: Literally 'see life with the woman you love': raah (H7200) as tasting, drinking in. The hebel-clause falls twice, and the wife is named inside it deliberately -- brevity is the argument for love, not against it. She is cheleq (H2506), portion, the same word God's gifts have carried all book long.

10.text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength; for there is no work, no reckoning, no knowledge, and no wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.
10.amp: Whatsoever your hand [yad] finds [matsa] to do [asah], do it with your might [koach]; for there is no work [maaseh], nor device [cheshbon -- reckoning, planning], nor knowledge [daat], nor wisdom [chokmah], in the grave [sheol], whither you go [halak].
10.notes: koach (H3581), full strength: mortality as fuel rather than paralysis. The four nouns denied to sheol (H7585) -- maaseh, cheshbon (H2808), daat, chokmah -- are the book's whole working vocabulary; every one of them is a now-word, and the door is closing.

11.text: I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not won by the swift, nor the battle by the strong; bread does not come to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favor to men of skill -- for time and chance meet them all.
11.amp: I returned [shub], and saw [raah] under the sun [shemesh], that the race is not to the swift [qal], nor the battle [milchamah] to the strong [gibbor], neither yet bread [lechem] to the wise [chakam], nor yet riches to men of understanding [bin], nor yet favour [chen] to men of skill [yada], but time [et] and chance [pega] happen [qarah] to them all.
11.notes: Five meritocracies overturned in one sentence: speed, strength, wisdom, understanding, skill. pega (H6294) is the unforeseen occurrence, and qarah (H7136) the befalling-verb -- yet in a book where every et (H6256) is appointed (3:1), 'chance' names man's blindness to the schedule, not the absence of one.

12.text: For man does not even know his own time. Like fish seized in a cruel net, like birds caught in the snare, so the sons of man are snared by an evil time when it falls on them suddenly.
12.amp: For man [adam] also knows [yada] not his time [et]: as the fishes that are taken [achaz -- seized] in an evil [ra] net, and as the birds that are caught [achaz] in the snare [pach]; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time [et], when it falls [naphal] suddenly [pitom] upon them.
12.notes: achaz (H270), the seizing-verb, twice: fish and fowl are going about their day in the instant the mesh closes. The 'evil et' is any hour of sudden calamity, and its signature is pitom (H6597), suddenness -- one more reason verse 10 says now.

13.text: I have also seen this example of wisdom under the sun, and it loomed large to me:
13.amp: This wisdom [chokmah] have I seen [raah] also under the sun [shemesh], and it seemed great [gadol] unto me:
13.notes: gadol (H1419), great: the little story that follows struck the Preacher as one of the weightiest things his survey turned up -- a parable of wisdom's power and wisdom's wages in the same four verses.

14.text: There was a little city with few men in it, and a great king came against it, surrounded it, and built massive siegeworks against it.
14.amp: There was a little [qatan] city [ir], and few [meat] men [enosh] within it; and there came [bo] a great [gadol] king [melek] against it, and besieged [savav -- surrounded] it, and built [banah] great bulwarks [matsod -- siegeworks] against it:
14.notes: Every word is sized for contrast: qatan (H6996) city, meat (H4592) men, gadol king, gadol bulwarks. savav (H5437), the surrounding-verb: the noose of the siege drawn around a town that has nothing -- except one resident.

15.text: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and he delivered the city by his wisdom. Yet not a soul remembered that same poor man afterward.
15.amp: Now there was found [matsa] in it a poor [misken] wise [chakam] man [ish], and he by his wisdom [chokmah] delivered [malat] the city [ir]; yet no man [adam] remembered [zakar] that same poor [misken] man.
15.notes: malat (H4422), the escape-word of 7:26, here worked by chokmah at city scale: one misken (H4542), one poor man, outweighed the siege-engines. The sting is zakar (H2142) negated -- the town he saved could not keep his name a season.

16.text: So I said, wisdom is better than strength; and still the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words go unheard.
16.amp: Then said [amar] I, Wisdom [chokmah] is better [tov] than strength [geburah]: nevertheless the poor man's [misken] wisdom is despised [bazah], and his words [dabar] are not heard [shama].
16.notes: Both clauses are true at once, and the book refuses to drop either: chokmah outperforms geburah (H1369), might -- and the world still filters wisdom by the wallet of the speaker. bazah (H959), to despise: the crowd's contempt does not lower wisdom's value, only their access to it.

17.text: The words of the wise, spoken quietly, are heard better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
17.amp: The words [dabar] of wise [chakam] men are heard [shama] in quiet [nachat] more than the cry [zaaq -- the shout] of him that rules [mashal] among fools [kesil].
17.notes: nachat (H5183), the quietness-word of 4:6 and 6:5: wisdom's native volume. The ruler's zaaq (H2201) fills the square and empties in an hour; the quiet dabar of the chakam keeps working in whoever truly did shama (H8085), hear it.

18.text: Wisdom is stronger than weapons of war, yet a single sinner destroys much good.
18.amp: Wisdom [chokmah] is better [tov] than weapons [keli] of war [qerab]: but one [echad] sinner [chet] destroys [abad] much [rabah] good [tov].
18.notes: The chapter's verdict and its warning in one breath: chokmah outranks the arsenal (keli, H3627, qerab, H7128), and yet the arithmetic of ruin is asymmetric -- echad chet (H259, H2398), one sinner, can abad (H6) what many wise men built. Guarding the good takes all of them; losing it takes one.
